If we have four identical spatial dimensions and the only thing that distinguishes the one we call time is that it is expanding at an astounding speed, the primary impact on force propagation is a radical asymmetry in how those forces are resolved by the worldlines living in that space.
The first major effect is what you might call temporal dilution. In a static 4D block, a force would propagate as a symmetric ripple in all directions. But because the time axis is stretching so much faster, any force ripple traveling along that dimension is going to be drawn out. Think of it like trying to paint a circle on a piece of rubber while someone is suddenly and violently stretching the rubber in one direction. The circle becomes an extremely long, thin ellipse. In the context of our filaments, this means that a high frequency oscillation in the spatial dimensions might be experienced as a very slow, low frequency gradient along the time dimension.
This expansion acts like a natural frequency filter. Because the time dimension is expanding at c, it essentially sets the shutter speed for the universe. Any force that propagates at a speed lower than the expansion rate gets left behind in the past, and any force that would have tried to propagate toward the past is effectively fighting an impossible headwind. This is where we get the illusion of causality. It is not that forces cannot travel pastward in 4D space—they can, because the dimensions are identical—it is just that the expansion of the lattice is so dominant that pastward signals are instantly washed out or pinned to the point of origin.
Another consequence is the conversion of wavelength into internal frequency. We see this in the way the framework treats neutrinos and photons. If a filament has a specific helical pitch—a vibration in 4D—and you rotate that filament so its long axis aligns more with the expanding time dimension, that spatial wavelength doesn't just disappear. It gets compressed into the time-like extent of the filament. From our 3D perspective, we no longer see it as a wave stretching through space; we experience it as an internal clock or a flavor oscillation frequency. The expansion of time essentially eats the spatial extent of the force and turns it into a rate of change.
There is also the matter of projective resistance or geometric blackout. As that one dimension expands, it creates a constant torque on any structure that isn't perfectly aligned with it. This is the winch effect we discussed. Forces that are perfectly balanced in 4D will eventually hit a geometric corner as the expansion of the time dimension forces the worldlines to precess. Once a force-carrying ripple precesses past that 14 degree threshold, it can no longer satisfy the gauge requirements of our 3D slice. It is still there in the 4D block, but it has been rotated into a dark state. The expansion of time is essentially the mechanism that blinks the lights of the universe on and off.
Ultimately, if the dimensions are identical and only the expansion rate differs, then force propagation is really just a study of how a 4D signal is Doppler-shifted by the expansion of the medium it is traveling through. What we call the laws of physics are just the specific interference patterns that manage to stay stable and visible against that relentless stretching. It makes the universe feel less like a collection of different forces and more like a single 4D sound that is being heard through an incredibly fast moving window. The different forces we see are just the different ways that one sound gets distorted as it passes through the expansion.
